title: Team AI Governance Without Bureaucracy
description: Create practical team rules for AI usage: what is allowed, what requires approval, and how to protect data while still moving fast.

data.text: Most organizations need AI guardrails, but heavy policy documents fail in practice. Effective governance is short, clear, and directly tied to daily decisions: what data can be pasted, which tools are approved, and when human sign-off is mandatory.

items.text: Approved tools list (and tools explicitly not approved)
Data classification rules (public / internal / sensitive / restricted)
Allowed and disallowed AI use cases by risk level
Human review requirements for high-impact outputs
Incident reporting path for AI mistakes or leaks

rows: Low risk; human editor still reviews
Uploading customer PII to free chatbot

data.caption: Route decisions by risk level so teams move quickly on low-risk work and escalate only when needed.

data.title: Governance that works
points: Keep policy short and operational (1-2 pages)
Focus on decisions people make daily
Classify data first, then decide tool usage
Add mandatory review for high-impact outputs
Revisit policy monthly as tools and risks evolve

cards.title: Lightweight
cards.description: Short policy, risk-tiered approvals, monthly refresh. Teams understand it and follow it because it is practical.

cards.title: Heavyweight
cards.description: Long policy documents, central approval for everything, annual review. Teams ignore it and use shadow AI because it is too slow.

data.title: Real team policy example
data.content:
A 12-person marketing team adopted this 1-page policy:

1. Approved tools: Claude Pro, Notion AI, Zapier. Everything else needs sign-off.
2. Data rules: Public content is fine. Internal docs are fine in enterprise tools. Customer PII never goes to a chatbot.
3. High-impact outputs: Any customer-facing content needs a 5-minute human review before publishing.
4. Incident path: If AI output leaks data or looks wrong, Slack #ai-ops within 1 hour.

Result: 80% adoption in 3 weeks, zero incidents in 2 months.

data.title: Common pitfall
data.text: The biggest governance mistake is writing a policy no one reads. Keep it under 2 pages, use examples, and revisit it monthly. A short policy that people follow beats a long policy that everyone ignores.

data.title: Remember
data.text: Governance is not the enemy of speed. Good governance removes uncertainty and lets teams move faster because they know what is allowed without asking for permission every time.
